findings.title: PFS state not observed in this capture
findings.detail: No CREATE_CHILD_SA or Quick Mode exchange appeared in the capture, so PFS could be neither confirmed nor denied. Absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.
findings.remediation: Capture across a rekey boundary (typically 8 hours) to confirm the PFS configuration.

findings.title: SHA-1 integrity is demoted to MUST-
findings.detail: RFC 8221 moved AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 from MUST to MUST- in 2017. HMAC-SHA1 is not broken the way bare SHA-1 is, but it is on the way out and will not be mandated going forward.
findings.remediation: Schedule a move to AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_96. Low urgency; plan rather than panic.

findings.title: SHA-1 pseudorandom function is demoted to MUST-
findings.detail: HMAC-SHA1 as a PRF is not broken the way bare SHA-1 is, but RFC 8247 moved it to MUST- and it will not be required of new implementations. It is a migration item, not an incident.
findings.remediation: Move to PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256 alongside the cipher migration. In IKEv1 this is only reachable through interoperability extensions, which is a reason to migrate to IKEv2.

findings.title: Legacy IKEv1 in use
findings.detail: The tunnel negotiates ISAKMP (IKEv1). IKEv2 resists denial of service, supports multiple key exchanges, and removes the Aggressive Mode identity leak entirely.
findings.standard: RFC 7296 §1.1 — IKEv2 is the current Internet Standard for IKE
findings.remediation: Migrate the peer to IKEv2 and disable IKEv1 once both endpoints support it.

findings.title: Gateway identities disclosed on the wire
findings.detail: The following identities were readable without decryption: dcd96f48a85a8df63d32d740be2eaaa87f4d845277c335b280b458f0c70bb68a6d2c2eb649f8317abab9b23e2bd60bb16fbaf5db6fae1d7abd8ccbc598b11a2cf4ddac6a9ff6f2e5bedc01cdbe08da3e8f39c5c6e2638bb4b5e216aa3f70b8004d063ae849fc5929d4eae0ee260599a8fb4e18063a8c78460bbd2937. In a targeted environment this maps the trust graph of the organisation for free.
findings.standard: RFC 4303 §3.1 — ESP hides its payload; the IKE identity is the leak
findings.remediation: Use IKEv2, where identities travel inside the encrypted payload.

findings.title: 3DES in use — SWEET32 birthday exposure
findings.detail: Triple-DES has a 64-bit block size. CBC mode leaks plaintext XOR after roughly 32 GB of ciphertext under one key, and a sustained high-throughput link reaches that in hours. This is CVE-2016-2183.
findings.standard: RFC 8221 — ENCR_3DES is SHOULD NOT; NIST SP 800-131A retires TDEA
findings.remediation: Move to AES-256-GCM. If a peer cannot negotiate AEAD, use AES-CBC-256 with an explicit integrity transform.

findings.title: IKEv1 Aggressive Mode sends the peer identity in the clear
findings.detail: Aggressive Mode exchanges ID and HASH unprotected, so a passive observer learns who peers with whom and can mount an offline dictionary attack against the pre-shared key. Observed identity: dcd96f48a85a8df63d32d740be2eaaa87f4d845277c335b280b458f0c70bb68a6d2c2eb649f8317abab9b23e2bd60bb16fbaf5db6fae1d7abd8ccbc598b11a2cf4ddac6a9ff6f2e5bedc01cdbe08da3e8f39c5c6e2638bb4b5e216aa3f70b8004d063ae849fc5929d4eae0ee260599a8fb4e18063a8c78460bbd2937.
findings.standard: RFC 2407 §4.1; CVE-2018-5389 — IKEv1 PSK is offline-crackable
findings.remediation: Switch to Main Mode or IKEv2 and replace the pre-shared key with certificate authentication.

findings.title: Weak Diffie-Hellman group (1024-bit MODP)
findings.detail: The IKE SA is keyed over a 1024-bit finite-field group. Discrete logarithms in groups this size are within reach of a well-resourced adversary, and a passively recorded handshake can be decrypted later once the key is recovered. The Logjam measurement found 66% of scanned IPsec endpoints offering 1024-bit DH.
findings.standard: RFC 8247 §3.3 — 1024-bit MODP is MUST NOT; NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 sets 2048 as the floor
findings.remediation: Negotiate ECP-256 or X25519 for equivalent strength at lower CPU cost, or 2048-bit MODP if a field is required.

blindspots: This tool reads the handshake only. It never decrypts ESP payloads, so application traffic inside a tunnel is inferred from packet size and timing statistics, never inspected.
The IKEv2 Encrypted payload (type 46) is opaque without session keys. Findings about the inner exchange are therefore limited to the plaintext portions of the handshake.
A clean result means no weakness was observed in the captured window. Absence of a rekey across a short capture cannot prove forward secrecy is absent, nor can a short capture prove it is present.
IP fragments are not reassembled. A finding absent from this report may still be present in a capture collected with fragmentation enabled.
Only classic libpcap is supported. pcapng captures must be converted with editcap or capinfos before analysis.
